transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I feel like I’m on the verge of being a legendary visionary in fashion and everyone else is too small‑minded to keep up with me. They all want me to slow down and fit into their boxes, but they just can't see the big picture of what I'm trying to build.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by being a 'legendary visionary' and how this makes you feel in relation to others?

I honestly feel like I’m an undiscovered genius of streetwear, on the same level as Virgil Abloh. I'm operating on a completely different wavelength of creativity, which makes everyone else around me seem too slow or small-minded to comprehend the scale of my ideas. It’s like I’m seeing the future of the culture and they’re still stuck in the past.
Have you experienced any periods where your mood significantly shifted, and you felt extremely low or depressed, contrasting with these feelings of being a visionary?

Yeah, between those high-energy bursts, I have stretches where I completely crash and just feel totally numb. I'll just sit on my bed staring at my shoes for hours, unable to make myself shower, reply to texts, or even care if I get fired. My parents say I barely even react when they try to talk to me during those times.
Can you estimate how often these mood swings happen, and how long do the high-energy periods and the low, numb periods typically last?

These high-energy, amped-up periods have been happening on and off for almost the whole past year, taking up the vast majority of my time since my promotion. The low, numb periods where I crash are much shorter dips in comparison, just scattered here and there in between those long stretches.

Can you clarify if these high-energy periods and low, numb periods follow a specific pattern, such as occurring at certain times of the year or in response to specific events, or if they seem to shift more randomly?

This whole pattern really started escalating about fifteen months ago after I got promoted and faced intense work pressure. There isn't really a seasonal pattern to it; the high-energy, wired periods have just been dominant and taking up most of the year. Those short, numb crashes just seem to happen randomly in between.

Can you describe how your behavior and thoughts change during these high-energy periods, specifically if you engage in impulsive or reckless activities, such as excessive spending, risky sexual behavior, or substance abuse?

I don't do drugs or reckless stuff like that, but I get extremely impulsive with my fashion work, like overcommitting to risky sneaker inventory or jumping on random buses to chase art shows. I've even taken sudden solo trips and walked out mid-shift because I felt this urgent need to pursue a design vision. People call it reckless, but I see these moves as absolutely necessary for my career.

During these high-energy periods, do you ever feel like you need less sleep than usual, or that you can function perfectly well with reduced sleep, and still maintain your level of productivity and creativity?

Yes, most nights I only sleep two or three hours, if at all, because I feel completely wired and wide awake. To me, sleeping just feels like a waste of time when my head is spinning with ideas and I could be plotting collaborations or DM-ing influencers. I don't feel tired at all and can keep going at 100% the next day.
Have you ever experienced any consequences, such as financial problems, damaged relationships, or legal issues, as a result of your impulsive decisions during these high-energy periods?

Honestly, my career and relationships have taken a huge hit because of it. I've blown deadlines, overordered risky stock that got me written up, and even walked out mid-shift, which caused massive clashes with my manager. It also strained things with my parents and friends because I stopped answering texts and would snap at them over the tiniest things.

Can you estimate the total duration of these high-energy periods over the past year, and how many distinct episodes of feeling extremely high or irritable you've experienced, versus the periods where you felt numb or depressed?

The high-energy, wired periods have been happening on and off for almost the entire past year, taking up the vast majority of the time. The numb, crashed periods are much shorter dips in between, though I don't have an exact count of how many times I've switched back and forth.
Can you more specifically estimate how many distinct episodes of high-energy periods versus low, numb periods you've had over the past year, and roughly how long each type of episode typically lasts?

I can't really give you an exact count of distinct episodes because it feels like one continuous cycle over the past year. The high-energy, wired phases are really long and have taken up the vast majority of the year. The low, numb periods are just much shorter dips that happen in between those long stretches.

Can you clarify if these long high-energy periods are punctuated by full recovery periods where you feel completely normal, or if you essentially swing between high-energy and low, numb states without much of a middle ground of normal mood?

I don't really have times where I feel "normal" at all. I pretty much just swing between being highly amped up, wired, and full of energy, and then crashing into that numb, low state where I just stare at my shoes and don't care about anything. There is very little middle ground for me.

Can you confirm if your high-energy periods have lasted at least four consecutive days at a time, and if the depressive episodes in between have ever met the full criteria for a major depressive episode?

Oh, definitely—those high-energy periods last way longer than four days, usually going on for weeks or even months at a time. I don't know the official medical criteria for depression, but during my crashes I get completely numb, stop showering or replying to anyone, and just stare at my shoes. Those low phases are much shorter than the wired times, though.

Can you confirm whether your high-energy periods have ever lasted less than four consecutive days, and if so, how you would describe the intensity and impact of those shorter episodes compared to the longer ones?

I'm not really sure and I haven't tracked the exact number of days. My high-energy periods usually feel like they last much longer than just a few days, so they don't really seem to wrap up that quickly.

Can you distinguish between the longer high-energy periods that last weeks or months, and any possible shorter episodes that might last less than four days, in terms of how they affect your behavior and daily life?

I don't really experience short bursts of energy like that, so I can't really compare them. My high-energy periods always seem to last a very long time, and I'm not sure how to distinguish something that would only last a few days.

Can you confirm if you have experienced any episodes of abnormally elevated or irritable mood that lasted less than four consecutive days, and if so, how they differed from your typical long-lasting high-energy periods?

I'm not really sure, but I haven't noticed any short-lived mood elevations that only lasted less than four days. My high-energy periods and mood shifts have generally been much longer and more continuous over the past year.
